lines.speaker: King Little
lines.text: Your Majesty.

lines.speaker: King Bombo
lines.text: Thank you, Your Majesty.

lines.speaker: King Bombo
lines.text: Marriage Contract.

lines.speaker: King Bombo
lines.text: King Little...

lines.speaker: King Bombo
lines.text: ...of Lilliput does this 5th day of November 1699 give the hand of his daughter, Princess Glory...

lines.speaker: King Bombo
lines.text: ...to Prince David, son of Bombo, King of Blefuscu.

lines.speaker: King Bombo
lines.text: Quite in order, right.

lines.speaker: King Bombo
lines.text: King... Bom... bo!

lines.speaker: King Bombo
lines.text: Well, we did it, you little rascal, you. We did it!

lines.speaker: King Little
lines.text: Yes, we certainly did, didn't we?

lines.speaker: King Bombo
lines.text: Just a couple of old dad cupids, I think.

lines.speaker: King Little
lines.text: A couple of old dad cupids!

lines.speaker: Bartholomew
lines.text: Well, you followed?

lines.speaker: Reggie
lines.text: Yes, by Dyle, but I lost him.

lines.speaker: Reggie
lines.text: I'm beginning to think women make the best spies.

lines.speaker: Bartholomew
lines.text: Agents.

lines.speaker: Reggie
lines.text: He has a gun, Mr. Bartholomew.

lines.speaker: Bartholomew
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Reggie
lines.text: But I saw it.

lines.speaker: Bartholomew
lines.text: No, that's not Carson Dyle.

lines.speaker: Reggie
lines.text: Carson?

lines.speaker: Bartholomew
lines.text: There's only one Dyle connected with this affair, Mrs. Lampert, that's Carson Dyle.

lines.speaker: Reggie
lines.text: You mean you've known about him all along?

lines.speaker: Bartholomew
lines.text: It's enough to make you a vegetarian, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Reggie
lines.text: It's just lucky that I'm not hanging next to one of those things right now.

lines.speaker: Reggie
lines.text: Why didn't you tell me you knew about Dyle?

lines.speaker: Bartholomew
lines.text: I didn't see any point. Dyle's dead.

lines.speaker: Reggie
lines.text: Mr. Bartholomew, what is all this about?

lines.speaker: Henderson
lines.text: And while on a hunting trip, my father discovered what are now known as the Henderson Caverns.

lines.speaker: Henderson
lines.text: More than 40 years ago, he mysteriously disappeared while exploring them further.

lines.speaker: Henderson
lines.text: Recently I found these maps and charts he left, suggesting there are still greater wonders and mysteries lay beyond in this vast underground world.

lines.speaker: Henderson
lines.text: Now if your paper will help finance the expedition, I will take Miss Lane and Mr. Kent with me and guarantee the Daily Planet exclusive rights to the story.

lines.speaker: Clark Kent
lines.text: Sounds like a great story, Chief.

lines.speaker: Lois Lane
lines.text: I'd love to go.

lines.speaker: Mr. White
lines.text: Well, let me see...

lines.speaker: Mr. White
lines.text: All right, it's a deal.

lines.speaker: Henderson
lines.text: Thanks, Mr. White. We can leave immediately.

lines.speaker: Barbra
lines.text: They ought to make the day the time changes the first day of summer.

lines.speaker: Johnny
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Barbra
lines.text: Well, it's eight o'clock and it's still light.

lines.speaker: Johnny
lines.text: A lot of good the extra daylight does us. Now we've still got a three-hour drive back. We're not going to be home until after midnight.

lines.speaker: Barbra
lines.text: Well, if it really bugged you, Johnny, you wouldn't do it.

lines.speaker: Johnny
lines.text: You think I wanna blow Sunday on a scene like this? You know, I figure we're either gonna have to move Mother out here or move the grave into Pittsburgh.

lines.speaker: Barbra
lines.text: She can't make a trip like this.

lines.speaker: Johnny
lines.text: Oh, I know that she can't.

lines.speaker: Johnny
lines.text: Is there any of that candy left?

lines.speaker: Barbra
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Johnny
lines.text: Look at this thing. "We still remember." I don't. You know, I don't even remember what the man looks like.

lines.speaker: Barbra
lines.text: Johnny, it takes you five minutes.

lines.speaker: Johnny
lines.text: Yeah, five minutes to put the wreath on the grave and six hours to drive back and forth. Mother wants to remember, so we trot 200 miles into the country and she stays at home.

lines.speaker: Barbra
lines.text: Well, we're here, John, all right?
